meta_title: Area of Ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 (NCERT Ex 8.1 Q4)
meta_desc: Solve the NCERT Class 12 area of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 (Ex 8.1 Q4), then test yourself with a free 8-question integration quiz with answers.

quiz.title: Area of an Ellipse Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding area by integration, built around the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 from NCERT Ex 8.1 Q4. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Area bounded by an ellipse using definite integration

questions.q: For the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, what are the lengths of the semi-major and semi-minor axes?
questions.explanation: The denominators are the squares of the semi-axes: 16 = 4² and 9 = 3², so a = 4 along the x-axis and b = 3 along the y-axis.

questions.q: Solving x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 for the upper half, y equals which expression?
questions.explanation: y² = 9(1 − x²/16) = 9(16 − x²)/16, so y = (3/4)√(16 − x²) for the part above the x-axis.

questions.q: The equation 9x² + 16y² = 144 becomes which standard form when divided by 144?
questions.explanation: Dividing every term by 144 gives 9x²/144 + 16y²/144 = 1, which simplifies to x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 — the same ellipse.

questions.q: The total area enclosed by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: For an ellipse the area is πab. Here a = 4 and b = 3, so the area is π × 4 × 3 = 12π square units.

questions.q: The area of just the first-quadrant quarter of this ellipse equals:
questions.explanation: By symmetry each quadrant holds one quarter of the total. 12π ÷ 4 = 3π square units.

questions.q: To get the whole area, the first-quadrant integral (3/4)∫₀⁴ √(16 − x²) dx is multiplied by:
questions.explanation: The ellipse is symmetric about both axes, so the first-quadrant area is repeated in all four quadrants — multiply by 4.

questions.q: The standard result ∫₀ᵃ √(a² − x²) dx equals:
questions.explanation: This integral gives the area of a quarter-circle of radius a, which is πa²/4. With a = 4 it evaluates to 4π.

questions.q: For a general ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1, its area is:
questions.explanation: The area of an ellipse is πab. When a = b it reduces to πa², the familiar area of a circle of radius a.

faq.q: What is the area bounded by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1?
faq.a: The area is 12π square units. Here a = 4 and b = 3, and the area of any ellipse is πab, so π × 4 × 3 = 12π.

faq.q: How is 9x² + 16y² = 144 the same as x²/16 + y²/9 = 1?
faq.a: Divide both sides of 9x² + 16y² = 144 by 144. You get x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, so both equations describe the identical ellipse.

faq.q: Why do we integrate only the first quadrant and then multiply by 4?
faq.a: The ellipse is symmetric about both the x-axis and the y-axis, so all four quadrants have equal area. Finding one quarter and multiplying by 4 keeps the working short and the limits simple (0 to 4).

faq.q: Which is longer, the major or the minor axis of this ellipse?
faq.a: Since 16 > 9, the ellipse stretches further along the x-axis. The semi-major axis is a = 4 (along x) and the semi-minor axis is b = 3 (along y).
